title: English
summary: About 10 questions: vocabulary (synonyms/antonyms), grammar and sentence correction, idioms, prepositions, analogies, short comprehension. Accuracy here is cheap marks.
definitions: Singular subjects take singular verbs; 'each', 'every', 'either', 'neither', 'everyone' are singular.
Verb agrees with the nearer subject.
Hypothetical conditions: 'If I were you…' for all persons.
look forward to meeting, object to being, used to working.
facts: Correlatives: hardly/scarcely … when; no sooner … than; not only … but also; both … and.
Latin comparatives (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior, prefer) take 'to', not 'than'.
'The number of' + singular verb; 'a number of' + plural verb.
Uncountable nouns with singular verbs: news, information, advice, furniture, equipment, luggage.
Fixed prepositions: good at, fond of, accused of, charged with, comply with, insist on, divided into, absent from, prefer to.
Redundancies to avoid: revert back, return back, repeat again, cousin brother.
Narration: past reporting verb back-shifts tense (am → was, will → would); pronouns change.
Passive of present continuous: is/are being + past participle.
traps: 'One of those engineers who ARE' — the verb agrees with 'engineers'.
Antonym questions sometimes include a synonym as a distractor — read the instruction.
